newsitem.title: INDONESIA: U.N. envoy hopeful after visit to East Timor.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy hopeful after visit to East Timor.

text.p: The United Nations special envoy for East Timor ended his first visit to the troubled territory on Monday and said prospects for a settlement were encouraging.

"There is a desire for a solution to this problem...this has been conveyed to me in my conversations at the highest levels," Jamsheed Marker said at the end of a 48-hour visit to the former Portuguese colony that Indonesia annexed in 1976.

Jakarta says East Timor has been fully integrated into Indonesia and has rejected demands by many in the territory for self-determination or more autonomy. Portugal has backed calls for self-determination.
"I do believe there is a desire, and, God willing, a possibility (for a solution)," Marker told Reuters.
U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Anan appointed Marker as special envoy for East Timor last month in an effort to swiftly resolve the row between Indonesia and Portugal over the territory.
U.N.-sponsored talks between the two nations have achieved little in 15 years.

Residents estimate more than 200,000 people have died since the Indonesian invasion of East Timor in 1975, a subsequent famine and two decades of Jakarta's suppression of the territory's self-determination movement.
Marker visited Lisbon earlier this month and was in Jakarta last week. He is to visit Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas later this week.
On Sunday, a group of youths, mainly students, demonstrated at the hotel in East Timor's capital of Dili where Marker was staying. At least 48 of them were arrested after brief scuffles.

East Timor police chief Colonel Jusuf Muharam told Reuters on Monday that three people has been released from custody. He said about 10 of 11 injured people remained in hospital, but he denied there had been any deaths or serious injuries.
Muharam said there was another brief demonstration on Monday but protesters dispersed after 30 minutes and there were no arrests. Residents described Dili as calm and normal on Monday.
Muharam said police seized 12 machettes and knives and 19 banners in Sunday's demonstration.
"There were 11 people injured whom we took to hospital. About 10 remain in hospital," Muharam said.
"Those who were injured broke the glass as they were leaving (the hotel) or were trampled on by others," Muharam said.
"There was only one warning shot and one tear gas canister fired. The warning shot was a rubber bullet to calm the crowd and stop them from becoming violent," he said.
Marker said he was in his room at the time of Sunday's demonstration and did not see what happened.
"There have been some reports that I refused to meet the students. This is not true," he said. "(The students) did not ask to meet me. I did ask the authorities to exercise lenience."
Marker said he formed impressions of the human rights situation in East Timor but would report on that to the secretary-general.

He also said he met Nobel Peace Prize laureate Bishop Carlos Belo, the most influential leader in Roman Catholic-dominated East Timor, and flew to Baucau town to meet the newly installed bishop of the Baucau diocese, Basilio do Nascimento.
